issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Pneumatic.openValve() with no parameters, but the solution implementation of the Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration). This parameter mismatch between the specification (problem statement) and the solution will confuse students about the correct method signature they must implement and may cause tests or expected implementations to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.openValve method signature consistent with the UML and problem statement by removing the duration parameter from the interface in the solution (openValve()) and update all implementing classes accordingly; alternatively, if the parameter is intended, update the problem statement UML to include openValve(int duration) so all artifacts match.

issues.description: Within the solution repository there is an internal inconsistency: the Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration) while the implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) override openValve() with no parameters. This mismatch means the solution code as provided does not compile and will prevent students from using it as a correct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signatures inside the solution: either change Pneumatic.openValve(int duration) to openValve() in the interface and keep the no-arg overrides, or change the overrides in LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster to openValve(int duration). Prefer matching the UML (openValve() with no parameters) so the solution compiles and matches the specification.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Pneumatic.openValve() as a no-argument method, but the Solution's Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration). Meanwhile the solution's concrete classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement openValve() with no arguments. This mismatch between the UML (problem), the Solution interface, and the implementing classes creates a confusing and inconsistent mapping for students and can cause compilation or test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.openValve method signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the Solution's Pneumatic interface to declare openValve() with no parameters (to match the UML and the implementing classes), or (B) update the UML and the concrete classes to use openValve(int duration). Also update the template Pneumatic.java to reflect the chosen signature so students see a consistent API.
